Module 05: Selection Pressure Engine

Evolutionary pressure shapes pathogen genomes, driving the emergence of diagnostic escape mutations. Module 05 calculates codon-specific selection pressures (\(dN/dS\) ratios) using the HyPhy (Hypothesis Testing using Phylogenies) software suite (Pond et al. 2020).

By identifying sites under purifying (negative) selection, the pipeline targets positions that are evolutionarily stable, ensuring long-term diagnostic assay durability.

1. Diversity-Aware Subsampling & Reading Frame Extraction

Because molecular evolutionary selection models scale non-linearly with sequence counts, the pipeline partitions sequence data before selection profiling:

  1. Diversity-Aware Subsampling (scripts/hyphy_subsample.py): Subsamples the global MSA into a representative subset (default: 50 to 2000 sequences) using a balanced stratification strategy based on subtype x country x year metadata. This maintains evolutionary diversity while reducing the computational load from thousands to a few hundred sequences.
  2. Coding-Gene Extraction (scripts/extract_genes.py): Slices the nucleotide sequence alignments into distinct open reading frames (ORFs) based on the CDS coordinate annotations in the input GFF3 file (e.g., extracting \(M1\) and \(M2\) genes for the Influenza A MP segment).
  3. Harsh Masking: Codons containing frame-breaking insertions, deletions, or high rates of ambiguous bases (\(N\)) are masked out. This step is critical because codon selection analyses require gap-free, in-frame codon triplets (length divisible by 3) to execute.
  4. Phylogenetic Tree Pruning (scripts/prune_tree.py): Prunes the main dated tree (tree.nwk) to only retain the tips present in the subsampled gene alignment, preventing tree-alignment dimension mismatches.

2. Selection Pressure Profiling Models

The engine executes two complementary selection models to discover mutations:

2.1. Pervasive Selection Analysis (FUBAR)

Pervasive (constant) selection pressure across the entire phylogeny is calculated using the FUBAR (Fast Unconstrained Bayesian Approximation) model (Murrell et al. 2013):

  • Objective: Computes the posterior probability of non-synonymous (\(dN\)) and synonymous (\(dS\)) substitution rates per codon site.
  • Purifying Selection: Codon positions with \(dN/dS < 1\) (specifically \(dN < dS\) with a posterior probability threshold \(\ge 0.9\)) are classified as conserved sites under negative selection. These sites are the primary targets for diagnostic primer and probe design.

2.2. Episodic Selection Analysis (MEME)

Periodical or branch-specific selection pressure is modeled using the MEME (Mixed Effects Model of Episodic Selection) model (Murrell et al. 2012):

  • Objective: Detects individual codon sites subject to episodic diversifying selection (positive selection occurring on only a subset of lineages/branches).
  • Relevance: Identifies hotspots where transient mutations arise (e.g., vaccine escape or antiviral resistance sites), which must be flagged as high-risk regions to avoid in diagnostic design.

3. Configuration & Execution Commands (Tabset Examples)

Below are the configuration parameters and terminal commands of Module 05:

  • 1. Configuration (config_influenza_a_mp.yaml)
  • 2. FUBAR Run Command
  • 3. MEME Run Command
  • 4. Output: FUBAR JSON Snippet
# [M05] Evolutionary Selection Pressure (HyPhy)
hyphy:
  threads: 8                      # Number of CPU threads assigned to HyPhy
  p_value_threshold: 0.1          # Significance threshold for positive selection
  methods:
    - "FUBAR"
    - "MEME"
  target_genes:
    - "ALL"                       # Process all CDS genes detected in GFF
  subsample:
    enabled: true                 # Subsample dataset to optimize HyPhy compute
    max_sequences: 2000
    min_sequences: 50
    strategy: "balanced"          # Balanced metadata distribution
    group_by:
      subtype: true
      country: true
      year: true
    seed: 42

Note the cache clearing step to prevent dimension mismatches from previous runs:

# 1. Clear stale cache files
rm -f results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m05/cleaned_M1_NT.fasta.FUBAR.cache

# 2. Run HyPhy FUBAR
hyphy CPU=8 fubar \
    --alignment results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m05/cleaned_M1_NT.fasta \
    --tree results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m05/tree_M1.nwk \
    --output results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m05/fubar_M1.json
# 1. Clear stale cache files
rm -f results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m05/cleaned_M1_NT.fasta.MEME.cache

# 2. Run HyPhy MEME
hyphy CPU=8 meme \
    --alignment results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m05/cleaned_M1_NT.fasta \
    --tree results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m05/tree_M1.nwk \
    --output results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m05/meme_M1.json

This snippet illustrates the FUBAR output JSON format, detailing the synonymous/non-synonymous rates and selection probabilities per codon position (e.g. index 0 represents codon 1):

{
  "analysis": {
    "info": {
      "model": "FUBAR",
      "sequences": 300,
      "codons": 252
    }
  },
  "MLE": {
    "headers": [
      ["alpha", "Synonymous substitution rate (dS)"],
      ["beta", "Non-synonymous substitution rate (dN)"],
      ["beta-alpha", "dN - dS"],
      ["prob_positive", "Posterior probability of positive selection (dN > dS)"],
      ["prob_negative", "Posterior probability of negative selection (dN < dS)"]
    ],
    "content": {
      "0": [
        [0.85, 0.12, -0.73, 0.01, 0.94],
        [1.12, 0.05, -1.07, 0.00, 0.98],
        [0.94, 2.45, 1.51, 0.92, 0.02]
      ]
    }
  }
}

3. Configuration & Parameterization

The selection pressure modeling is constrained by sequence limits and statistical cutoffs defined in config.yaml:

# [M05] Selection Pressure (HyPhy)
hyphy:
  max_sequences: 300              # Limit of sequences to run in HyPhy to prevent time explosion
  min_sequences: 50               # Minimum sequences required to run HyPhy
  seed: 42                        # Subsample seed for selection pressure
  fubar_threshold: 0.90           # Posterior probability cutoff for purifying selection (dN < dS)
  meme_threshold: 0.05            # P-value cutoff for episodic selection (dN > dS)

3.1. Parameter Tuning Dictionary

Parameter Name Allowed Values Default Value Purpose & Biological Meaning
hyphy.max_sequences Integer 50 to 2000 300 HyPhy’s FUBAR and MEME computations scale non-linearly with sequence count. Setting a limit of 300 sequences balances statistical accuracy and execution speed (averaging ~10 minutes per run). Increasing this beyond 1000 can lead to days of computation on standard CPUs.
hyphy.min_sequences Integer \(\ge 10\) 50 The minimum sample size. Below 50 sequences, the statistical power of FUBAR is insufficient to resolve site-by-site selection patterns safely.
hyphy.fubar_threshold Float 0.5 to 1.0 0.90 The posterior probability cutoff. Codons with a FUBAR probability \(\ge 0.90\) for \(\text{dN} < \text{dS}\) are flagged as highly conserved and under strong purifying selection.
hyphy.meme_threshold Float 0.0 to 1.0 0.05 The significance level (p-value). Codons with a MEME p-value \(\le 0.05\) are flagged as undergoing episodic positive selection (mutational hot-spots).

3.2. How to Interpret HyPhy JSON Outputs

Module 05 outputs raw JSON files (fubar_M1.json and meme_M1.json):

  • FUBAR Columns: Look for the parameters alpha (synonymous rate, \(dS\)) and beta (non-synonymous rate, \(dN\)). If beta is close to 0 and prob_negative is high (\(\ge 0.90\)), this site is extremely stable and a gold-standard target for diagnostic design.
  • MEME Columns: Look for p-value. A low value indicates that at least one branch of the phylogenetic tree has experienced sudden diversification. These coordinates must be avoided.

4. Inputs, Outputs & Files

The files involved in Module 05 are summarized below:

File Role Path Format Description
Input Alignment results/{build}/m03/aligned.fasta FASTA Full sequence alignment from Module 03.
Input Tree results/{build}/m04/tree.nwk Newick Dated timetree from Module 04.
Subsampled Fasta results/{build}/m05/aligned_hyphy.fasta FASTA Subsampled FASTA sequences.
Extracted Gene results/{build}/m05/cleaned_{gene}_NT.fasta FASTA Extracted coding gene sequences (in-frame).
Pruned Tree results/{build}/m05/tree_{gene}.nwk Newick Pruned phylogenetic tree matching the gene subset.
FUBAR Output results/{build}/m05/fubar_{gene}.json JSON dN/dS ratios and posterior probability stats.
MEME Output results/{build}/m05/meme_{gene}.json JSON Episodic diversifying selection statistics.

5. Troubleshooting & Limitations

5.1. HyPhy Stale Cache Dimension Mismatches

  • Problem: HyPhy exits with a fatal error: Index out of range or Matrix dimensions do not match.
  • Cause: When running FUBAR or MEME, HyPhy automatically generates and reads a binary cache file (e.g. *.FUBAR.cache) in the input folder. If you rerun the pipeline with a different number of sequences, the old cache size will conflict with the new alignment.
  • Solution: The Snakemake pipeline resolves this by programmatically purging any existing *.cache files in the output directory before invoking HyPhy.

References
